heuristics: H1: the 128-bit hash of the canonical x-coordinate, from which the table index (bits 0..15 of lane a) and the distinguished test (bits 16..63 of lane a and 0..49 of lane b) are read, behaves as a random oracle on the visited classes; its instruction cost is charged and no claim is made about bits of the coordinate itself.

H2: the class walk collides like a uniform random function on N_eff = 1.10^2 (1+1/2^16) N' classes (standard additive-walk penalty plus an explicit 10% allowance in steps; the budget is 1.15 sqrt(1+1/2^16) k0). Teske 2001 covers ordinary r-adding walks, not this exact quotient walk; toy-scale runs of the exact walk are supporting evidence only.

H3: closing patterns of the class walk follow the random model: formal closures need every used table index at least twice (exact bound Q(L) for any units); canonical units are uniform and independent for lengths above 8192; non-formal closure has probability at most 6/r per start and length. Undetected cycles of length above 64 trap a walker with total probability at most 2^-27.9, subtracted from success; detected cycles are charged at 300 units per event and at most 2^-14 events per step.
limitations: Analytic accounting; no full-size execution; the toy experiment covers groups of 390 to 21710 classes with tables of 16 or 64 entries and is supporting evidence only.
Costs use the fixed reference prices C=2000 and 383 instructions per Fp multiplication; per-step instruction counts are itemised estimates (640) with a reserve (750 charged).
Memory of about 2^36.5 bytes is needed for the distinguished-point store; memory carries no score.
Not a novel attack: textbook parallel collision search with automorphisms. No theorem covers the exact walk; success rests on H1-H3.
